slides.heading: Malaria
slides.subtitle: A parasitic infection transmitted by the night-biting female Anopheles mosquito.

slides.heading: Vector — Female Anopheles flavirostris
bullets: Breeds in clear, flowing, shaded streams.
Brown-colored and bigger than other species.
Night-biting (10 PM–4 AM); does not bite a person in motion.

slides.heading: Nursing Management by Stage
rows: Warm blankets (prevent hypothermia), paracetamol, hydration, start ACT antimalarials
Tepid sponge bath/cooling, hydration, paracetamol, continue antimalarials
Rehydration (replace fluid lost), rest & monitoring, nutritional support

slides.heading: Prevention
bullets: 4 S's: Search & destroy, Seek early consultation, Self-protection, Support fogging.
Repellents: DEET, Picaridin, Oil of Lemon Eucalyptus; treat nets twice a year.
Biologic control: mosquito fish (Gambusia), Tilapia, frogs; neem & eucalyptus.
TREC: Treatment, Report (weekly), Early detection, Casefinding.

slides.heading: Key Takeaways
bullets: Plasmodium via the night-biting (10 PM–4 AM) female Anopheles flavirostris.
Diagnose with a malarial blood smear.
Three clinical stages: cold → hot → sweating; treat with ACT.
